title: Operator-facing audit summaries and signoff prototype
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working sketch for a compact, operator-oriented summary layer above raw audit logs for Private deployments. The key idea: produce short, actionable signoff summaries that let a human operator (or on-call reviewer) quickly approve or escalate network/edge config changes without reading mega-log blobs. This is targeted at customer-managed networking handoffs where compliance teams want a crisp statement of risk and evidence.

Why this exists (problem we see):
- Raw audit logs are voluminous and noisy. Operators waste time searching for the few items that matter for an approval decision.
- Current approval gates rely on full log artifacts or dense evidence bundles that take hours to inspect.
- Customers expect human-readable rationale + small evidence artifacts for retention/cost reasons.

High-level goals:
- Generate a one-screen summary per change attempt that answers: what changed, who requested it, what automated checks passed/failed, signal of blast radius, top-3 risk indicators, and recommended signoff level.
- Keep the summary small (<= 3 short paragraphs + 5 bullets + 1 compact evidence link).
- Provide both machine- and human-friendly views: machine fields for automation + natural-language paragraph for operator.
- Maintain cryptographic linkage to full audit bundle for forensic needs.

Non-goals (for now):
- Full formal proof-of-authority cryptographic protocol (we will surface existing signed receipts instead).
- Replacing full forensic workflows. This is for triage/signoff, not for post-incident root cause.

Proposed summary structure (single record fields):
- summary_id: short hash (derived from change id + timestamp)
- change_handle: tenant-id / change-id / requestor
- one_line: short descriptive sentence (eg "Added egress rule to allow 10.2.3.0/24 → redis:6379")
- risk_level: low | medium | high (derived heuristics)
- reasons: 1-3 bullets listing why that risk level was set (eg: new wide-open CIDR, public egress, privileged port)
- critical_checks: list of named checks and pass/fail (eg: k8s-pod-ownership:pass, dns-allowlist:fail)
- blast_radius_est: small numeric score 0-10 and brief rationale
- sample_evidence_urls: 1-2 short links (immutable bundle id, replay token, compressed trace)
- recommended_action: allow | allow-with-monitoring | escalate | deny
- human_summary: 2-4 sentences in plain language for operator signoff

Compression heuristics for log -> summary mapping (notes/ideas):
- Prefer semantic deltas (config diff) over append-only logs. We compute a compact diff snapshot and phrase it as the one_line.
- Keep the top-3 risk indicators using ranked signals: exposed-cidr-size, protocol/port sensitivity, credential-change flag, IAM-privilege-escalation, CI-notary-mismatch.
- Where possible, convert quantitative signals into discrete bins (eg CIDR size -> host / small-subnet / org-subnet / public) so operators read quickly.
- If multiple checks fail, prefer escalate/deny; if only informational checks flagged, suggest allow-with-monitoring.

Operator UI sketch (quick notes, for Console PM/UX):
- Header: one_line + risk pill (color coded) + change_handle + timestamp. Quick expand: human_summary + toggle to see machine fields.
- Central area: small diff view (collapsed) + top-3 reasons. Each reason has a "why this matters" short tooltip.
- Right rail: compact evidence card (bundle id, size, signed-by, retention TTL), recommended action buttons (Allow / Allow+Monitor / Escalate) and audit checkbox (I reviewed this because...).
- Persistent option: attach a short operator rationale note (free text) that gets included into the signoff record.

Signoff record format (what we persist when operator clicks Allow/Escalate):
- signoff_id: string
- actor: name + identity provider id
- action: allow | allow-with-monitoring | escalate | deny
- operator_note: free text (optional)
- linked_summary_id: string
- evidence_bundle_id: string
- signed_receipt: short signed token from control plane
- retention_policy_tag: short label (eg: "audit-7y", "ephemeral-30d")

Integration points (who/what needs to feed this):
- Network change service: change diffs and raw logs (already exists as change_id).
- Approval engine: hook that decides whether to auto-approve or route to operator flow. Use JIRA-PRIV-1873 to track rule updates.
- Telemetry/Observability: small sample traces to estimate blast radius (link to metrics).
- Forensics: S3/immutable store of the full evidence bundle with content-addressable id.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- For a given set of 10 replayed sample changes (pilot customers + internal), the summary must include a correct one_line description in >= 90% of items and risk_level agreement with SME in >= 80%.
- UI: operator can complete signoff (allow/deny/escalate) in <= 2 minutes for low-risk and <= 7 minutes for medium-risk test cases.
- Every signoff record stores a cryptographically-linked bundle id and operator note.

Retention and cost tradeoffs (notes for infra):
- We surface compact evidence URL; full bundle remains in object storage. To save cost, proposed retention tiers: audit-1y for high-risk; audit-90d for medium; audit-30d for low with option to escrow to customer-managed S3.
- Summaries themselves are tiny and searchable — retain 3y by default.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2w): instrument summary generator and produce dry-run outputs for internal SRE + 1 pilot customer. No UI, only API payloads.
- Phase 1 (4w): Console UI prototype + acceptance criteria testing with SRE/product reviewers.
- Phase 2 (6w): Beta with 3 pilot customers (customer-managed VPC + small enterprise). Collect operator timings and false positives.
- Phase 3: GA with retention/TOS updates and toggle for customer to opt into operator-signoff UI.

Security and compliance notes:
- Signoff actions are auditable and must be immutable after creation (append-only).
- Operator notes must be redaction-friendly (PII might be present in raw logs). Provide a redact tool for evidence bundles before sharing externally.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: final mapping of heuristics to risk_level; assign to Jamal (PRIV-helm ticket).
- TODO: retention labels and customer opt-out semantics — coordinate with Legal.
- Q: Should recommended_action be deterministic or ML-recommended with confidence band? (tradeoffs: explainability vs fewer clicks)
- Q: How to model multi-change rollups? Operators sometimes want to sign off on a batch window — need PV for grouping.

Appendix — sample generated summary (raw text example):
summary_id: s-3b2f9c
change_handle: tenant-acme / ch-20250212-99 / alice@acme.com
one_line: "Added egress 0.0.0.0/0 -> redis:6379 from namespace payments"
risk_level: medium
reasons:
- public egress to redis port
- namespace has service-account with cross-tenant binding (previously flagged)
- no recent vulnerability scan attached to image
critical_checks: k8s-ownership:pass, dns-allowlist:fail, iam-binding:warn
blast_radius_est: 6 (namespace + service-account)
sample_evidence_urls: [bundle://s3/priv/evidence/2025/02/ch-99.tar.gz]
recommended_action: escalate
human_summary: "The change opens public egress to redis on port 6379 from the payments namespace. The change touches a service-account that has a cross-tenant binding previously marked. We recommend escalation for deeper review; minimal monitoring will likely miss cross-account exfil patterns."

---
Notes: this is intentionally a prototype doc with rough UX/acceptance ideas. Goal is to converge on a compact schema we can emit from control-plane and hook into Console. Reach out in #priv-controlplane or drop comments on the linked PR for implementation decisions.

Last edited by: Marina Velasquez
